title: Idempotency token collision causing tenant-visible 5xx bursts; graded shedding & retry suppression plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a recent customer escalation one tenant observed spikes of 5xx responses and timeouts correlated with aggressive client retries. Investigation shows a pattern where idempotency tokens emitted by older SDK versions collide across ephemeral proxy frontends, causing request de-duplication to fire incorrectly and evict critical KV cache entries. The eviction combined with concurrent retries led to long tail KV compaction and transient backend work that pushed some serving workers over cpu/io thresholds, producing 5xx waves and client-visible timeouts.

Impact: multiple customers reported elevated error rates and higher latency for generation endpoints for ~45 minutes. The issue is scoped to Hosted (edge/ingress proxy + router) but has implications for Dedicated when similar proxy topologies are used. Private deployments may be unaffected unless configured with the same idempotency scoping.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Some SDKs generate idempotency tokens with low entropy and predictable prefixes when instantiating clients in short-lived worker pools.
- Frontend proxy hashing logic uses the full token as a routing key across connection pools; collisions cause unrelated requests to be deduplicated and map to the same in-flight work item.
- Dedup/multiplex path added a KV cache eviction side-effect when an in-flight slot is waited on; eviction compaction is synchronous under heavy pressure and stalls worker loop.
- Concurrent retries from clients amplify the effect, creating retry storms that increase queueing and timeouts.

Proposed mitigation and plan of record:
1) Immediate mitigation (hotfix, customer-facing):
   - Disable cross-tenant idempotency deduplication at the proxy layer for Hosted within 30 minutes. This reduces incorrect dedup and prevents eviction cascade. (rollback prepared)
   - Apply temporary per-tenant connection/admission limiter to cap concurrent in-flight per-tenant requests to safe default (20).
   - Notify affected customers with mitigation status and ETA for fix.

2) Short-term fixes (next 1-2 sprints):
   - Patch router to scope idempotency token namespace by tenant + endpoint hash before dedup decisions.
   - Change dedup implementation to use weak references and async compaction to avoid synchronous KV eviction on wait path.
   - Add server-side token entropy checks and log telemetry when low-entropy tokens observed (metric: low_entropy_token_rate).
   - SDK guidance: publish breaking change to recommend UUIDv4 tokens and add opt-in enforcement in latest SDKs.

3) Long-term improvements (Q2+):
   - Per-tenant adaptive admission controller that integrates with billing priority and Dedicated reservation to allow dynamic headroom.
   - Rolling guardrail: circuit-breaker that converts excess retries into fast-fail with suggestive Retry-After and idempotency guidance.
   - End-to-end reproducibility tests (chaos + replay) covering dedup, eviction, and retry amplification scenarios.

Instrumentation and observability work:
- New dashboards: low_entropy_token_rate, dedup_eviction_rate, per-tenant_inflight_count, dedup_wait_latency_p95. Links in comments below.
- Alerts: dedup_eviction_rate > 1/min for > 5m for any tenant -> P0 oncall; per-tenant_inflight_count > threshold -> auto-shed.

Rollback criteria:
- If disabling dedup increases cost or reduces throughput beyond acceptable SLAs for a tenant and impacts customers negatively, revert and apply admission limiter only.

Testing and rollout strategy:
- Canary rollout in two stages: infra-internal tenants -> a small set of low-risk customers -> all Hosted. Provide a canary gate (metric-based) that fails if dedup_wait_latency_p95 increases by >10%.
- Unit and integration tests for token scoping and async eviction in runtime test harness.

Cross-team coordination:
- Notify PMs and Solutions Eng for customer communication and account-level mitigations.
- Design: update SDK docs and error guidance copy.

Deliverables / artifacts:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4762 (dedup scoping change)
- Playbook: confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Idempotency+Collision+Incident
- Postmortem: draft in confluence link above (assigned to Aisha Patel)
